# Move Countdown: Calendar Reminders

**Instructions:** Set your move date as Day 0. Count backward. Copy each entry as a calendar event. I've kept titles short so they read well on a phone lock screen. Set each as an all-day event or at the suggested time, whichever you prefer.

---

**WEEK 8 (56–50 days before move)**

**Day 56 — Monday morning, 9 AM**
Title: MOVE — Send lease notice / list house
Who: Joint
Notes: Send written notice to landlord (certified mail or email with read receipt). If selling, confirm listing date with realtor. Keep a copy of everything.

**Day 55 — Tuesday morning, 10 AM**
Title: MOVE — Get 3–4 mover quotes
Who: Joint
Notes: Contact at least 3 licensed interstate movers. Request in-home or video estimates. Verify USDOT numbers on FMCSA SAFER site. Also price U-Haul, Penske, and PODS for comparison.

**Day 54 — Wednesday morning, 9 AM**
Title: MOVE — Book vet visit for dog
Who: M
Notes: Schedule a checkup. Ask for copies of all records, rabies certificate, vaccine history, microchip number, and any travel medication if the dog gets carsick.

**Day 53 — Thursday, 12 PM**
Title: MOVE — Research Oregon housing
Who: M
Notes: Set search filters, bookmark listings, join local rental groups. If renting remotely, check if the landlord accepts video tours and digital signing.

**Day 52 — Friday afternoon, 2 PM**
Title: MOVE — Vehicle decision: drive or ship?
Who: Joint
Notes: Get 2–3 vehicle shipping quotes if considering it. Compare cost of shipping vs. driving both cars vs. selling one. Factor in the dog riding with you.

---

**WEEK 7 (49–43 days before move)**

**Day 49 — Monday morning, 9 AM**
Title: MOVE — Compare mover quotes and decide
Who: Joint
Notes: Review all quotes. Check for binding vs. non-binding, valuation coverage, and cancellation terms. Decide: full-service movers, hybrid, DIY truck, or container.

**Day 48 — Tuesday morning, 10 AM**
Title: MOVE — Book mover or reserve truck
Who: Joint
Notes: Lock in the date and pay the deposit. Read the contract before signing. Save confirmation number and contact info. If DIY, reserve truck or container now.

**Day 46 — Thursday, 11 AM**
Title: MOVE — Book vehicle shipping (if applicable)
Who: M
Notes: Confirm pickup window, open vs. enclosed, and what to remove from the car before pickup. Save carrier name, phone, and booking number.

**Day 45 — Friday morning, 9 AM**
Title: MOVE — Start gathering documents
Who: Joint
Notes: Pull together titles, registrations, insurance cards, birth certificates, passports, lease, medical records, prescriptions, tax returns. Put them in one folder.

---

**WEEK 6 (42–36 days before move)**

**Day 42 — Monday morning, 9 AM**
Title: MOVE — Confirm Oregon housing
Who: Joint
Notes: Sign lease or confirm closing. Save lease copy to your Move folder. If not confirmed yet, set a hard deadline for end of this week and have a backup plan (extended-stay hotel).

**Day 41 — Tuesday, 10 AM**
Title: MOVE — Schedule Oregon internet install
Who: P
Notes: Internet installs can take 2+ weeks to schedule. Call now and book for the day you arrive or the day after. Save confirmation.

**Day 40 — Wednesday, 10 AM**
Title: MOVE — Map Ohio utility shutoffs
Who: M
Notes: List every utility (electric, gas, water, trash, sewer, internet, cable). Note each provider's shutoff notice requirement. Schedule shutoffs for the day after move day.

**Day 39 — Thursday, 10 AM**
Title: MOVE — Map Oregon utility startups
Who: M
Notes: Call or go online for electric, gas, water, trash at the new address. Schedule start dates to match your arrival. Save confirmation numbers.

**Day 38 — Friday afternoon, 2 PM**
Title: MOVE — Begin declutter: garage and storage
Who: Joint
Notes: Sort into keep, sell, donate, trash. Post sellable items on Facebook Marketplace or Craigslist this weekend. Schedule donation pickups.

---

**WEEK 5 (35–29 days before move)**

**Day 35 — Monday morning, 9 AM**
Title: MOVE — File USPS change of address
Who: Joint
Notes: Go to usps.com. Set the forwarding start date for about 2 days before your move so mail catches up. Costs about $1.10 to verify identity online.

**Day 34 — Tuesday, 10 AM**
Title: MOVE — Notify banks, credit cards, insurers
Who: Joint
Notes: Update your mailing address with every bank, credit card, health insurance, auto insurance, and any loan servicers. Update beneficiary addresses if needed.

**Day 33 — Wednesday, 11 AM**
Title: MOVE — Start packing: storage rooms and guest room
Who: Joint
Notes: Pack anything you won't use in the next 4 weeks. Label every box with room name and contents. Number the boxes and keep a simple list on your phone.

**Day 32 — Thursday, 2 PM**
Title: MOVE — Book dog-friendly lodging for the drive
Who: M
Notes: Plan 2–3 overnight stops. Book pet-friendly hotels along I-80 or your chosen route. Confirm pet fees and weight limits. Save confirmation numbers.

**Day 30 — Saturday, 10 AM**
Title: MOVE — Buffer: confirm all bookings
Who: Joint
Notes: Call or check confirmations for mover or truck, vehicle shipper, Oregon housing, hotels on route, internet install. Flag anything unconfirmed and fix it today.

---

**WEEK 4 (28–22 days before move)**

**Day 28 — Monday morning, 9 AM**
Title: MOVE — Order packing supplies
Who: P
Notes: Boxes (small, medium, large, wardrobe), packing tape, bubble wrap, markers, mattress bags. Ask grocery and liquor stores for free boxes this week too.

**Day 27 — Tuesday, 10 AM**
Title: MOVE — Pack books, decor, off-season clothes
Who: Joint
Notes: Use small boxes for books. Wrap framed art in bubble wrap. Bag off-season clothes and label clearly.

**Day 26 — Wednesday, 10 AM**
Title: MOVE — Cancel or transfer subscriptions and services
Who: P
Notes: Gym, meal kits, newspaper, lawn care, pest control, security system, streaming with regional content. Cancel what you won't need. Transfer or pause the rest.

**Day 25 — Thursday, 2 PM**
Title: MOVE — Research Oregon DMV requirements
Who: M
Notes: Look up what you need for an Oregon license and vehicle registration: proof of identity, proof of residency, title, insurance, emissions test requirements. Save the checklist from the Oregon DMV site.

**Day 22 — Sunday, 6 PM**
Title: MOVE — Packing check-in
Who: Joint
Notes: Walk through the house together. What's packed, what's left? Are you on track? Adjust the plan for next week if behind.

---

**WEEK 3 (21–15 days before move)**

**Day 21 — Monday morning, 9 AM**
Title: MOVE — Pack kitchen (non-essentials)
Who: Joint
Notes: Pack anything you won't cook with in the next 2 weeks: baking supplies, extra dishes, small appliances, cookbooks. Keep one pot, one pan, a few plates, mugs, and utensils out.

**Day 20 — Tuesday, 10 AM**
Title: MOVE — Confirm mover details
Who: Joint
Notes: Call the mover or truck company. Confirm date, arrival window, crew size, payment method, and access instructions (stairs, elevator, parking). Get it in writing.

**Day 19 — Wednesday, 11 AM**
Title: MOVE — Car maintenance check
Who: M
Notes: Oil, tires, brakes, battery, fluids, wipers. If anything needs repair, get it done this week. You don't want surprises on I-80 through Wyoming.

**Day 18 — Thursday, 2 PM**
Title: MOVE — Pack bathrooms (non-essentials)
Who: Joint
Notes: Keep out 2 towels each, toiletries, cleaning supplies for the final clean. Pack everything else.

**Day 17 — Friday, 10 AM**
Title: MOVE — Update dog's ID tag
Who: M
Notes: Order or get a tag with your new Oregon address and your cell number. Attach it before the drive. Update microchip info after arrival.

**Day 15 — Sunday, 6 PM**
Title: MOVE — Buffer: donation and sell deadline
Who: Joint
Notes: Last call for selling or donating furniture and items. Anything not claimed by today should be posted as free or scheduled for trash pickup.

---

**WEEK 2 (14–8 days before move)**

**Day 14 — Monday morning, 9 AM**
Title: MOVE — Pack bedrooms (non-essentials)
Who: Joint
Notes: Leave out sleeping essentials, 3–4 days of clothes, chargers. Pack the rest. Put mattress bags on the beds on moving day.

**Day 13 — Tuesday, 10 AM**
Title: MOVE — Pack living room
Who: Joint
Notes: Leave out the TV if you want it for the last week. Pack books, games, photos, throws, lamps you've already replaced with overhead light.

**Day 12 — Wednesday, 10 AM**
Title: MOVE — Prep moving-day dog plan
Who: M
Notes: Decide: will the dog stay with a friend, go to daycare, or stay in a closed room on moving day? Book it now. Pack the dog's travel bag (food, bowls, leash, meds, toys, blanket, waste bags, vet records).

**Day 11 — Thursday, 2 PM**
Title: MOVE — Photograph valuables and serial numbers
Who: M
Notes: Take photos of electronics, furniture, and anything of value. Save serial numbers. Store on your phone and email yourself a copy.

**Day 10 — Friday afternoon, 3 PM**
Title: MOVE — Confirm vehicle shipping pickup (if applicable)
Who: M
Notes: Call the carrier. Confirm pickup date, location, and your contact number. Remove personal items and aftermarket accessories from the car. Note existing damage in photos.

**Day 9 — Saturday, 10 AM**
Title: MOVE — Assemble moving-day essentials box
Who: Joint
Notes: This rides in the car with you, not the truck. See the one-page essentials list. Include chargers, toiletries, 2 changes of clothes, dog supplies, documents folder, snacks, water, paper towels, trash bags, basic tools, first-aid kit, medications.

---

**WEEK 1 (7–1 days before move)**

**Day 7 — Monday morning, 9 AM**
Title: MOVE — Final packing push
Who: Joint
Notes: Everything except daily-use items should be boxed. If you're behind, today is catch-up day. Order pizza and power through.

**Day 6 — Tuesday, 10 AM**
Title: MOVE — Defrost fridge and freezer
Who: P
Notes: Unplug the fridge. Put towels under it. Donate or cook remaining perishable food. Clean it out.

**Day 5 — Wednesday, 10 AM**
Title: MOVE — Confirm all Oregon services are set to start
Who: M
Notes: Electric, gas, water, internet, renter's insurance. Call each one and confirm the start date and that the account is active.

**Day 4 — Thursday, 10 AM**
Title: MOVE — Final mover or truck confirmation
Who: Joint
Notes: Last call with the mover or rental company. Confirm arrival time, payment, and anything they need from you (clear path, parking, elevator reservation).

**Day 3 — Friday, 2 PM**
Title: MOVE — Pack the car
Who: M
Notes: Load the essentials box, documents folder, dog supplies, suitcases, valuables you don't want on the truck, snacks, and water. Leave room for the dog's crate or seat.

**Day 2 — Saturday, 6 PM**
Title: MOVE — Final night prep
Who: Joint
Notes: Set out clothes for tomorrow. Charge all devices. Pack the last toiletries in the morning. Set an alarm. Get some sleep.

**Day 1 — Sunday (or your move day)**

**6:00 AM**
Title: MOVE DAY — Wake up, final pack
Who: Joint
Notes: Pack the last toiletries, sheets, pillows. Bag trash. Eat breakfast.

**7:30 AM**
Title: MOVE DAY — Movers arrive (or start loading truck)
Who: Joint
Notes: Walk the crew through the house. Point out fragile items. Keep the dog secured away from the action.

**12:00 PM**
Title: MOVE DAY — Walkthrough and lockup
Who: Joint
Notes: After loading, do a full walkthrough. Open every closet, cabinet, and drawer. Photograph each room. Read meters and photograph them. Return keys and remotes. Lock up.

**12:30 PM**
Title: MOVE DAY — Hit the road
Who: Joint
Notes: First stop in 2 hours for the dog. Drive safe. You're doing this.

---

**POST-MOVE REMINDERS (set these now for after arrival)**

**Day +1**
Title: ARRIVED — Photograph new place and report damage
Who: Joint
Notes: Walk through every room. Photograph walls, floors, fixtures, appliances. Email the landlord with any existing damage within the timeframe your lease requires.

**Day +3**
Title: POST-MOVE — Oregon vet visit
Who: M
Notes: Bring all records. Get the dog established with a new vet. Ask about the county dog license.

**Day +7**
Title: POST-MOVE — Oregon DMV: license and registration
Who: M
Notes: Bring ID, proof of residency, vehicle title, insurance, and any required forms. Schedule the emissions test if needed.

**Day +10**
Title: POST-MOVE — Confirm everything transferred
Who: Joint
Notes: Check mail forwarding is working, all subscriptions updated, insurance active at new address, employer payroll updated, voter registration confirmed. Breathe.

turns.text:
# Room-by-Room Packing Checklist

**How to use this:** Work through each room in the order listed. The priority levels tell you when to pack each category relative to your move date. "Early" means 4–6 weeks out, "Mid" means 2–3 weeks out, and "Late" means the final week. Box counts assume standard medium (18×18×16) and small (16×12×12) boxes. Adjust for your actual volume. Time estimates assume two people working together at a steady pace without major interruptions.

---

## KITCHEN

**Estimated totals:** 12–20 boxes, 4–6 hours across two sessions

**Who:** Joint (this room has the most stuff and the most fragile items — do it together)

**Declutter first (1–2 hours, do this 4+ weeks out):**
Go through every drawer and cabinet before you pack a single box. Pull out everything you haven't used in the past year. That garlic press you forgot you owned, the chipped mugs, the duplicate spatulas, the novelty shot glasses from a road trip five years ago — let them go. Expired spices and food get tossed. Donate functioning appliances you won't miss. If you have more than two of something (can openers, colanders, cutting boards), keep the one you like best and pass the rest along. Be ruthless here because kitchen boxes are heavy and fragile, which means they're expensive to move and annoying to unpack.

**Early (4–6 weeks out) — Priority: Medium**

Category: Baking supplies and specialty cookware (bundt pans, roasting pans, pie dishes, cookie sheets you won't use before the move). Also pack cookbooks, entertaining dishes, serving platters, holiday dishware, fondue sets, and anything aspirational you haven't touched recently. Estimated boxes: 2–4 medium. Time: 45 min.

Category: Small appliances you won't use in the next month (bread maker, food processor, stand mixer, waffle iron, blender if you have a backup). Wrap cords around each appliance and secure with a rubber band. If you kept the original box, use it. Otherwise wrap in dish towels and bubble wrap. Estimated boxes: 1–3 medium. Time: 30 min.

**Mid (2–3 weeks out) — Priority: High**

Category: Most dishes, glasses, and mugs. Keep out 2 plates, 2 bowls, 2 mugs, and 2 glasses per person. Pack everything else. Wrap each glass and plate individually in packing paper or newsprint. Stand plates on edge in the box like records, not flat. Put glasses in cell dividers if you have them. Estimated boxes: 3–5 medium. Time: 1–1.5 hrs (this is the slowest part because of wrapping).

Category: Most utensils, tools, and gadgets. Keep out one chef's knife, one spatula, one wooden spoon, one can opener, tongs, and a peeler. Bundle silverware in rubber bands by type. Wrap sharp knives in cardboard sleeves or towels. Estimated boxes: 1–2 small. Time: 20 min.

Category: Pots and pans (keep out one pot and one skillet). Nest pans with paper between them to prevent scratching. Lids can go in a separate box or on top. Estimated boxes: 1–2 medium. Time: 20 min.

Category: Pantry food. Discard anything expired, opened and stale, or not worth the weight. Seal open packages in zip-lock bags. Pack cans and jars in small boxes (they get heavy fast — do not use large boxes for canned goods). Wrap glass bottles and jars individually. Estimated boxes: 2–4 small. Time: 30 min.

**Late (final week) — Priority: Critical**

Category: Last-use kitchen items. On the last full day in the house, pack the remaining plates, mugs, pot, skillet, utensils, dish soap, sponge, hand towel, trash bags, and paper towels. Put the dish soap and sponge in a zip-lock bag and tuck them into your moving-day essentials box so you can clean up at the new place on arrival. Estimated boxes: 1 small. Time: 15 min.

Category: Cleaning supplies under the sink. Pack or discard. Check which items movers won't transport (flammable or hazardous — lighter fluid, certain cleaners). If driving yourself, keep these in a separate clearly labeled box and transport upright. Estimated boxes: 1 small. Time: 15 min.

**Kitchen tips:** Line the bottom of every kitchen box with crumpled paper for cushion. Mark all kitchen boxes "FRAGILE — KITCHEN" on the top and two sides. Pack a "first meal" zip-lock in your essentials box with paper plates, plastic utensils, napkins, a corkscrew, and a couple of snack bars so you don't have to dig through boxes your first night.

---

## LIVING ROOM

**Estimated totals:** 6–12 boxes plus furniture, 2–4 hours across two sessions

**Who:** Joint for packing, P takes point on electronics and cables, M handles wall art and decor

**Declutter first (1 hour, do this 4+ weeks out):**
Take everything off the shelves and surfaces and sort it on the floor. Old magazines, DVDs you'll never rewatch, board games with missing pieces, candles burned down to nubs, decorative items you've stopped noticing — donate or discard. Books are the biggest trap: be honest about which ones you'll reread. If you haven't opened it since you moved in here, it probably shouldn't make the trip to Oregon. A box of books weighs 30–50 pounds, and you'll feel every one of them on that truck or invoice.

**Early (4–6 weeks out) — Priority: Low to Medium**

Category: Books. Use small boxes only. A medium box full of books will weigh 50+ pounds and the bottom will blow out. Fill small boxes about three-quarters full and use packing paper or a towel to fill the gap at the top. Alternate spine-in and spine-out for a tighter fit. Estimated boxes: 2–6 small. Time: 30–60 min depending on your collection.

Category: Decorative items, photo frames, vases, candles, knickknacks. Wrap frames in bubble wrap or towels. Put glass items in packing paper. Stand frames upright in the box, not flat. Estimated boxes: 1–3 medium. Time: 30 min.

Category: Media (CDs, DVDs, vinyl, games). If you've gone fully digital, now is the time to sell or donate physical media. Pack what you're keeping in small boxes. Estimated boxes: 1–2 small. Time: 20 min.

**Mid (2–3 weeks out) — Priority: High**

Category: Wall art, mirrors, and hanging decor. Take photos of your arrangement if you want to recreate it. Use picture boxes or make a cardboard sandwich (two pieces of cardboard taped around the frame). Mark "FRAGILE — DO NOT LAY FLAT" on each one. Remove nails and hooks from the walls and spackle the holes. Estimated boxes: 1–3 flat or specialty. Time: 30–45 min. (Who: M)

Category: Throw pillows, blankets, and curtains. These are great box fillers but can also go in large trash bags or vacuum-seal bags if you have them. Remove curtain rods and bundle the hardware in a labeled zip-lock taped to the rod. Estimated boxes: 1–2 large bags or boxes. Time: 15 min.

Category: Board games and puzzles. Rubber-band game boxes shut so lids don't pop off. Bag loose pieces. Estimated boxes: 1 medium. Time: 10 min.

**Late (final week) — Priority: Critical**

Category: Electronics. Photograph the back of your TV, router, and any entertainment setup so you know exactly which cable goes where. Coil each cable and label it with a small piece of tape. Pack remotes in a zip-lock bag labeled "LIVING ROOM REMOTES." If you still have original boxes for the TV or console, use them. Otherwise, wrap the TV in a moving blanket and transport it upright, never flat. If movers are handling it, ask them to use a TV box. Estimated boxes: 1–3 medium (not counting TV). Time: 30–45 min. (Who: P)

Category: Lamps. Remove bulbs and shades. Wrap shades in packing paper (don't use newsprint — the ink transfers). Wrap bases in bubble wrap. If the lamp is tall, consider whether it's worth moving or replacing in Oregon. Estimated boxes: 1–2 medium. Time: 15 min.

Category: Rugs. Roll, don't fold. Secure with twine or packing tape. If they're large, the movers can handle them or they can go on the truck floor. Estimated boxes: 0 (they're rolled). Time: 10 min.

**Living room tips:** Keep the couch, one lamp, and the TV set up until the last week if you need a place to relax after packing sessions. Disassemble furniture on the last day or let the movers do it. Put all hardware (screws, bolts, brackets) for each piece of furniture in a labeled zip-lock bag and tape it to the furniture itself.

---

## HOME OFFICE

**Estimated totals:** 5–10 boxes, 2–3 hours

**Who:** Whichever of you uses the office most takes the lead. Assign M or P based on whose workspace it primarily is. The other person helps with furniture and filing.

**Declutter first (1–2 hours, do this 4+ weeks out):**
Shred old documents you no longer need (bank statements older than 7 years unless relevant to taxes, old utility bills, expired warranties, old pay stubs if you have digital copies). Recycle old notebooks, dried-out pens, broken supplies, and tangled cables you can't identify. If you have old electronics (phones, tablets, laptops) collecting dust, wipe them and recycle them at a local e-waste drop-off. Test every pen and marker — throw away the dead ones.

**Early (4–6 weeks out) — Priority: Medium**

Category: Reference books, manuals, and binders you won't need before the move. Small boxes for books, medium for binders. Estimated boxes: 1–3 small. Time: 20 min.

Category: Archived files and tax records. Keep the last 3 years of tax returns accessible in your documents folder. Pack older records in a clearly labeled box. Consider scanning anything you're keeping purely for reference and storing it in the cloud. Estimated boxes: 1 medium file box. Time: 30 min (longer if you're scanning).

**Mid (2–3 weeks out) — Priority: High**

Category: Office supplies (staplers, tape, paper clips, sticky notes, printer paper, ink). Put small loose items in zip-lock bags. Estimated boxes: 1–2 small. Time: 15 min.

Category: Printer and scanner. Remove ink cartridges and bag them separately (they can leak). If you have the original box, use it. Otherwise, wrap in bubble wrap and pack snugly. Estimated boxes: 1 medium. Time: 15 min.

Category: Filing cabinet contents. If the cabinet is coming with you, leave files inside and tape drawers shut (lighter is better for the movers, though, so use your judgment). If not, transfer active files to a portable file box. Estimated boxes: 1–2 file boxes. Time: 20 min.

**Late (final week) — Priority: Critical**

Category: Computer, monitor, keyboard, mouse, and cables. Back up everything to an external drive or cloud before packing. Photograph cable connections. Coil and label each cable. Wrap the monitor in a moving blanket or bubble wrap. Transport the computer in the car if possible — temperature swings and vibration in a truck can damage hard drives. Estimated boxes: 1–2 medium plus the computer itself. Time: 30 min.

Category: Desk lamp, personal items, last-minute paperwork. Estimated boxes: 1 small. Time: 10 min.

**Office tips:** Your external hard drive or backup should ride in the car with you, along with any laptop you use daily. If you work remotely, coordinate your pack-up day with your last workday at the Ohio address so you're not trying to work off a phone while your desk is in a truck.

---

## MASTER BEDROOM

**Estimated totals:** 8–14 boxes plus furniture, 3–4 hours

**Who:** Joint. Each person packs their own clothes and personal items. Collaborate on shared items like bedding and furniture.

**Declutter first (1–2 hours, do this 4+ weeks out):**
Try on anything you're unsure about. If it doesn't fit, you don't like how it looks, or you haven't worn it in a year, donate it. This includes shoes. Most people move 30–40% more clothing than they actually wear. For each item, ask: would I buy this again today? If not, it goes. Check nightstands and dressers for junk-drawer accumulation — old chargers, expired medications, random coins, receipts. Under the bed is usually a graveyard of forgotten things. Clear it out now.

**Early (4–6 weeks out) — Priority: Medium**

Category: Off-season clothes. If it's warm, pack winter coats, boots, sweaters, and heavy layers. Use wardrobe boxes for hanging clothes if you want to avoid re-ironing everything. Vacuum-seal bags work well for bulky items like winter coats and save a lot of space. Estimated boxes: 2–4 wardrobe or large. Time: 30–45 min per person.

Category: Extra bedding, spare pillows, guest sheets. Vacuum-seal or pack in large bags or boxes. These make good padding around fragile items too. Estimated boxes: 1–2 large. Time: 15 min.

Category: Sentimental items (photo albums, keepsakes, jewelry you don't wear daily). Wrap carefully. Consider transporting jewelry and irreplaceable items in the car. Estimated boxes: 1 small. Time: 15 min.

**Mid (2–3 weeks out) — Priority: High**

Category: Most clothing. Leave out about a week's worth of outfits per person plus sleepwear. Pack the rest. Keep hangers on hanging clothes and drape a trash bag over a group of them (poke the hangers through the bottom of the bag) for a quick wardrobe-box alternative. Estimated boxes: 3–6 wardrobe or large. Time: 45 min–1 hr per person.

Category: Shoes. Stuff shoes with packing paper to hold their shape. Pair them with rubber bands. Use original boxes if you have them, or line them up in a medium box. Estimated boxes: 1–2 medium. Time: 15 min.

Category: Dresser drawers. If the dresser is coming with you and the movers are okay with it, you can leave soft items (socks, underwear, t-shirts) in the drawers and wrap the dresser in moving blankets. This saves boxes. Ask your movers first. Estimated boxes: 0 if leaving in drawers, 2–3 medium otherwise. Time: 10 min.

**Late (final week) — Priority: Critical**

Category: Last week's clothes. Pack into a suitcase that rides in the car with you. Include outfits for 3–4 days, sleepwear, underwear, socks, one layer for cold nights on the road. Estimated boxes: 0 (suitcase). Time: 15 min per person.

Category: Bedding in use. Strip the bed on moving morning. Stuff sheets and pillowcases into a trash bag or the mattress bag. Put the mattress bag on and tape it shut. Pillows can go in trash bags. Estimated boxes: 1 large bag. Time: 10 min.

Category: Nightstand essentials (phone charger, glasses, book, medication). These go in your moving-day essentials box or your personal bag. Estimated boxes: 0. Time: 5 min.

**Bedroom tips:** Label boxes by person if your clothes are going to different closets. Use suitcases and duffel bags you're already moving as packing containers for clothes and soft goods — no reason to leave them empty.

---

## SECOND BEDROOM / GUEST ROOM

**Estimated totals:** 4–8 boxes plus furniture, 1.5–2.5 hours

**Who:** P (or whichever of you uses this room less — it should be one of the first rooms fully packed and closed off)

**Declutter first (

turns.text:
## SECOND BEDROOM / GUEST ROOM (continued)

**Declutter first (1 hour, do this 4+ weeks out):**
Guest rooms tend to become catch-all spaces. Be honest about what's actually guest furniture and what's just stuff you didn't know where else to put. If the guest bed is old or low quality, consider whether it's worth the cost to ship it 2,400 miles or whether you'd be better off donating it and buying a replacement in Oregon. Same goes for a desk or futon you barely use. This is the room where people move the most things they never touch again. Everything in this room should earn its spot on the truck.

**Early (4–6 weeks out) — Priority: High (pack this room first and close the door)**

Category: Guest bedding, spare pillows, extra blankets. Vacuum-seal or bag them. These can be packed immediately since nobody is sleeping here before the move. Estimated boxes: 1–2 large bags. Time: 15 min.

Category: Anything stored in this room that belongs in another category (holiday decorations, luggage, craft supplies, old textbooks, exercise equipment). Sort it into the correct room's packing stream or into the donate/sell/trash pile. Estimated boxes: 2–4 medium. Time: 30–45 min.

Category: Closet contents. Guest room closets are storage closets in disguise. Pull everything out, lay it on the bed, and sort. Coats you forgot about, boxes you haven't opened since the last move, bags of things you meant to return — if you haven't needed it in the time you've lived here, you almost certainly don't need it in Oregon. Estimated boxes: 1–3 medium. Time: 30 min.

**Mid (2–3 weeks out) — Priority: Medium**

Category: Furniture disassembly. If you're taking the bed frame and any shelving, disassemble them now. Put all hardware in a labeled zip-lock bag and tape it directly to the frame piece it belongs to. Lean disassembled pieces against a wall. If the movers are disassembling for you, skip this but confirm they'll do it. Estimated boxes: 0 (zip-lock bags for hardware). Time: 20–30 min.

**Late (final week) — Priority: Low**

This room should already be empty and closed off. Use it as a staging area for packed boxes if you need the floor space. Walk through it one last time on moving day and check the closet shelf, any built-in drawers, and the ceiling light fixture (people leave bulbs and ceiling fan pull chains behind more than you'd think).

**Guest room tips:** Since this room gets packed earliest, it makes a good packing station. Keep your tape, markers, paper, and bubble wrap in here and work from this room outward.

---

## BATHROOM

**Estimated totals:** 3–5 boxes, 1–1.5 hours

**Who:** Joint. Each person packs their own toiletries. One person handles the medicine cabinet and linen closet.

**Declutter first (30 min, do this 3–4 weeks out):**
Check expiration dates on everything. Medications, sunscreen, contact lens solution, that bottle of cough syrup from 2021 — if it's expired, discard it properly (don't flush medications; many pharmacies accept them for safe disposal). Toss dried-out nail polish, crusty mascara, nearly empty bottles of anything, and hotel shampoo you're never going to use. Old towels that have gone scratchy can be donated to an animal shelter, which is a nice full-circle move given the dog.

**Early (4–6 weeks out) — Priority: Low**

Category: Spare towels and linens beyond what you're actively using. Keep 2 bath towels and 1 hand towel per person plus a bath mat. Pack everything else. Estimated boxes: 1 large bag or box. Time: 10 min.

Category: Backup toiletries and bulk supplies (unopened shampoo, extra toothbrushes, bulk soap, cotton balls). Estimated boxes: 1 small. Time: 10 min.

**Mid (2–3 weeks out) — Priority: Medium**

Category: Medicine cabinet contents you're not using daily. Pack non-daily medications, first-aid supplies, thermometer, heating pad, and supplements you can pause for a few weeks. Keep daily prescriptions, pain reliever, bandaids, and allergy meds accessible. Estimated boxes: 1 small. Time: 15 min.

Category: Under-sink storage. Cleaning supplies, extra toilet paper, hair tools you don't use often. Check what movers won't transport (aerosols, nail polish remover, rubbing alcohol — anything flammable). Transport those yourself or discard. Estimated boxes: 1 small. Time: 15 min.

Category: Shower and bath extras. If you have a shower caddy with six half-used bottles, consolidate. Keep one shampoo, one conditioner, one body wash, and one razor. Pack or discard the rest. Estimated boxes: 1 small. Time: 10 min.

**Late (final week) — Priority: Critical**

Category: Daily toiletries. On the last morning, pack your toothbrushes, toothpaste, deodorant, face wash, contacts, and any daily medication into a zip-lock bag. This goes in your moving-day essentials box or your personal overnight bag. Do not put this on the truck. Estimated boxes: 0 (overnight bag). Time: 5 min.

Category: Shower curtain, bath mat, last towels. Pull these on moving morning after everyone has showered. Roll the towels and stuff them in a trash bag. The shower curtain liner can be tossed if it's old. Estimated boxes: 1 bag. Time: 5 min.

Category: Toilet paper. Throw a roll in the essentials box. You will want it at the new place before anything else is unpacked. This is not a joke. Estimated boxes: 0 (essentials box). Time: 10 seconds.

**Bathroom tips:** Put all liquids in zip-lock bags before boxing them. Shampoo bottles and lotions pop open in transit and ruin everything they touch. Use towels and washcloths as packing material around fragile bathroom items like mirrors or glass soap dispensers.

---

## GARAGE

**Estimated totals:** 5–15 boxes plus loose items and large tools, 4–8 hours (this room takes the longest because of sorting)

**Who:** M takes the lead (or whoever uses the garage more). P assists with heavy lifting and sorting decisions.

**Declutter first (2–3 hours, do this 5–6 weeks out — start here before any other room if possible):**
The garage is where moves go to die. It's full of things you kept because you "might need them someday" and that day has not come. Be aggressive. Get four zones set up: keep and move, keep and sell, donate, and trash. Work through one section at a time — don't try to do the whole garage in one pass or you'll burn out.

Things to seriously consider not moving: half-used paint cans (movers won't take them and they're not worth the weight — note the color codes and buy new in Oregon), old lumber scraps, rusty tools that have better replacements available for $15 at a hardware store, broken holiday lights, that exercise bike you haven't touched, dried-out garden chemicals, and anything you've been meaning to fix for more than a year. Gasoline, propane tanks, motor oil, pesticides, and other hazardous materials cannot go on a moving truck and are often not worth transporting yourself. Dispose of them at your local hazardous waste facility and replace them in Oregon.

If you have power tools with value (table saw, miter saw, drill press), decide now whether to sell or move them. They're heavy and expensive to ship, but also expensive to replace. Price it out both ways.

**Early (4–6 weeks out) — Priority: High**

Category: Seasonal items you won't use before the move (holiday decorations, camping gear out of season, ski equipment). Estimated boxes: 2–4 large. Time: 30–45 min.

Category: Sporting goods and outdoor recreation (bikes, kayak accessories, fishing gear, golf clubs). Clean them before packing. Bikes can ride in the truck unboxed if the movers allow it, or disassemble the front wheel and pedals and wrap the frame. Estimated boxes: 1–3 medium plus loose items. Time: 30 min.

**Mid (2–3 weeks out) — Priority: High**

Category: Hand tools and hardware. Sort screws, nails, and small hardware into labeled zip-lock bags. Wrap sharp tools (saws, chisels) in cardboard or towels. Put hand tools in a sturdy box or a tool bag. Estimated boxes: 1–2 medium (heavy — keep them small). Time: 30–45 min.

Category: Power tools. Wrap cords, remove batteries, and pack in original boxes if available. If not, wrap in moving blankets and box. Transport lithium batteries in the car if possible, as extreme heat in a truck can be a concern. Estimated boxes: 1–3 medium. Time: 30 min.

Category: Garden tools (rakes, shovels, hoe, pruners). Bundle long-handled tools with twine or bungee cords. Wrap blades in cardboard. These often ride loose in the truck. Consider whether your Oregon yard will need the same tools — if you're moving from a house with a big lot to an apartment, you may not need them. Estimated boxes: 0 (bundled). Time: 15 min.

Category: Lawn mower. Drain the gas and oil before the move (movers require this, and it's safer for a DIY truck too). If the mower is old or low-value, it may cost more to move than to replace. Estimated boxes: 0 (loose). Time: 20 min.

**Late (final week) — Priority: Medium**

Category: Workbench items, shelving contents, last-pass sweep. By this point the garage should be mostly clear. Do a final pass for anything tucked behind shelves, in rafters, or on high hooks. Estimated boxes: 1–2 medium. Time: 20 min.

Category: Car supplies (jumper cables, tire inflator, emergency kit, ice scraper). The emergency kit goes in the car for the drive. The rest gets boxed. Estimated boxes: 1 small. Time: 10 min.

**Garage tips:** Photograph your garage before you start so you can see the progress. It's motivating. Rent a dumpster for a weekend if you have a lot to toss — it's usually $200–$400 and saves a dozen trips to the dump. Schedule a Habitat for Humanity ReStore pickup for large donated items like workbenches and shelving.

---

## STORAGE UNIT

**Estimated totals:** Varies wildly. Budget 3–6 hours for sorting and 2–4 hours for packing what you keep.

**Who:** Joint (block out a full Saturday for this)

**Declutter first (this is the whole point):**
If you're paying monthly for a storage unit, the move is the perfect reason to empty it completely. Here's the uncomfortable math: if you've been paying $75–$150 a month and the stuff has been in there for a year or more, you've already spent $900–$1,800 storing it. Is it worth that much? For most people, the answer is no for at least half of what's in there.

Pull everything out into the daylight. Make the same four piles as the garage: move, sell, donate, trash. Anything you forgot was in there is a strong candidate for not making the trip. Furniture you replaced, boxes from your last move you never opened, old electronics, duplicate kitchen items from when you combined households — let it go. If you find items with genuine sentimental or financial value, great, those go on the truck. Everything else should leave your life before you leave Ohio.

**Packing what survives the purge:**

Re-box anything in damaged or water-stained boxes. Check for mold or pest damage on soft goods like clothes and upholstery. If something smells musty, it's not going to improve in a truck for three days. Label everything clearly since these boxes tend to get shoved in last and opened last. Estimated boxes: 3–10 medium depending on what you keep. Time for packing: 2–4 hrs.

**Cancel the unit.** Give written notice per your rental agreement (often 30 days) and schedule a walk-through. Clean the unit and return the lock. Get your deposit back in writing. Add "cancel storage unit" to your calendar at the right time.

---

## HALLWAYS, ENTRYWAY, AND COAT CLOSET

**Estimated totals:** 2–4 boxes, 30–45 min

**Who:** P

**Declutter:** The coat closet is a time capsule. You'll find umbrellas you didn't know you had, a raincoat from three apartments ago, scarves you never wear, and shoes that migrated from the bedroom. Keep what you actually reach for when you walk out the door. Donate the rest.

**Mid (2–3 weeks out) — Priority: Low to Medium**

Category: Coats, jackets, scarves, hats, gloves. Keep one jacket each for the drive and pack the rest. Use a wardrobe box or large trash bag draped over hangers. Estimated boxes: 1 wardrobe or large bag. Time: 10 min.

Category: Shoes by the door, shoe rack. Pack all but the pairs you're wearing this week. Estimated boxes: 1 medium. Time: 10 min.

Category: Hooks, key holders, mail organizer, mirror. Take them down, spackle the holes, pack the items. Estimated boxes: 1 small. Time: 10 min.

**Late (final week) — Priority: Low**

Category: Welcome mat, umbrella stand, last coats. Roll the mat, grab the umbrellas, done. Estimated boxes: 0 (loose). Time: 5 min.

---

## LAUNDRY AREA

**Estimated totals:** 1–3 boxes, 30–45 min

**Who:** M

**Declutter:** Toss stained rags, old sponges, stretched-out drying racks, and laundry products that are nearly empty. If you have five different stain removers and none of them worked, they're not going to start working in Oregon.

**Mid (2–3 weeks out) — Priority: Medium**

Category: Cleaning supplies, mops, brooms, dustpan, vacuum bags, iron and ironing board. Keep the vacuum and one set of basic cleaning supplies for the final clean. Pack the rest. Wrap the iron's cord and let it cool completely before boxing. Estimated boxes: 1–2 small. Time: 15 min.

Category: Laundry supplies (detergent, dryer sheets, stain remover). Seal open containers in zip-lock bags. Liquid detergent is heavy and can leak — consider finishing what you have and buying new at the other end. Estimated boxes: 1 small. Time: 10 min.

**Late (final week) — Priority: Critical**

Category: Washer and dryer. If you own them and they're coming: run an empty cleaning cycle, disconnect hoses, and let the washer drain completely. Tape the power cord to the back. Secure the washer drum with transit bolts (check the manual or look up your model — this prevents internal damage during transport). The movers should know how to do this but confirm. If you don't own them, clean them out as a courtesy to the landlord and move on. Estimated boxes: 0. Time: 20 min for disconnect and prep.

Category: Last loads of laundry. Do your final loads 2 days before the move so everything is clean and dry for packing. The clothes you're wearing on moving day go in your overnight bag. Estimated boxes: 0. Time: just the laundry cycles.

Category: Drying rack, hamper, hangers. The drying rack folds flat and can go loose in the truck. Bag extra hangers with a rubber band. Estimated boxes: 0 (loose items). Time: 5 min.

---

## LINEN CLOSET (if separate from bathroom)

**Estimated totals:** 1–3 boxes or bags, 20 min

**Who:** P

**Declutter:** You do not need 14 towels for two people and a dog. Keep 4 bath towels, 4 hand towels, 2 washcloths each, and 2 sets of sheets per bed. Donate the rest. Old towels with fraying edges or stains can go to the animal shelter.

**Early (4–6 weeks out) — Priority: Low**

Pack everything except what you're actively using

## LINEN CLOSET (continued)

**Early (4–6 weeks out) — Priority: Low**

Pack everything except what you're actively using this month. Spare sheet sets, extra blankets, tablecloths, and napkin sets can go into vacuum-seal bags or large trash bags and be packed immediately. Use linens as padding around fragile items in other boxes to save on bubble wrap. Estimated boxes: 1–2 large bags or boxes. Time: 15 min.

**Late (final week) — Priority: Low**

Category: In-use sheets and towels. Strip and pack on moving morning after showers. Stuff them into a trash bag, label it, and toss it on the truck last so it comes off first if you need bedding that night. Estimated boxes: 1 bag. Time: 5 min.

**Linen closet tips:** Check the top shelf. It's where people hide gift wrap, heating pads, humidifiers, and first-aid kits they forgot about. Pull everything down and sort before you close this area out.

---

## FINAL NOTES ON THE ROOM-BY-ROOM PROCESS

**Labeling system that actually works:** Write three things on every box in large marker on the top and at least one side. First, the room it's going to in the new house (not where it came from — this is for the movers or for you on unload day). Second, a one-line summary of contents ("kitchen — plates and bowls, fragile"). Third, a number. Keep a running list on your phone with the box number and a quick note of what's inside. This sounds tedious but it takes five seconds per box and will save you an hour of opening and re-closing boxes when you're looking for the coffee maker at 7 AM on your first morning in Oregon.

**The "open first" boxes:** Pack one per room, labeled clearly with "OPEN FIRST" in a different color marker. These contain the things you'll need within the first hour of unloading: kitchen gets the coffee maker, dish soap, paper towels, and a few mugs; bedroom gets the sheets, pillows, and phone chargers; bathroom gets the toilet paper, hand soap, towels, and shower curtain.

**A word on pacing:** You don't have to do this in marathon sessions. Two focused hours in the evening, three or four times a week, will get a 2-bedroom packed in about 3 weeks without destroying your quality of life. Put on a podcast, work through one category at a time, and stop when the energy drops. Packing while exhausted leads to bad labeling, broken items, and fights about whose job it was to wrap the wine glasses.

# MOVING-DAY ESSENTIALS — One-Page Car Kit

*Print this page. Check each item off as it goes in the car. Everything on this list stays with you, not on the truck.*

**DOCUMENTS (M — gather the night before)**

- [ ] Driver's licenses and passports
- [ ] Vehicle title, registration, and insurance cards
- [ ] Moving contract, Bill of Lading, and inventory sheet
- [ ] Lease or closing papers for the new place (with landlord/agent phone number)
- [ ] Copies of medical prescriptions
- [ ] Dog's vet records, rabies certificate, and microchip number
- [ ] Cash ($200–$300 for tips, tolls, and emergencies)
- [ ] Phone chargers and a car charger

**CLOTHING AND PERSONAL (each person packs their own)**

- [ ] 3 days of clothes per person in a small bag or suitcase
- [ ] Sleepwear
- [ ] Comfortable driving shoes
- [ ] One warm layer each (mountain passes get cold even in summer)
- [ ] Toiletry kit: toothbrush, toothpaste, deodorant, face wash, contacts/glasses, daily medications
- [ ] Sunglasses

**FOOD AND WATER (P — pack morning of)**

- [ ] Cooler with water bottles, drinks, and cold snacks
- [ ] Non-perishable snacks (granola bars, trail mix, crackers, fruit)
- [ ] Paper plates, plastic utensils, napkins (for first meal at new place)
- [ ] Paper towels
- [ ] Trash bags (3–4, various sizes)

**DOG KIT (M — pack the night before)**

- [ ] Dog food (enough for 4 days) and treats
- [ ] Collapsible water and food bowls
- [ ] Water bottle or jug dedicated to the dog
- [ ] Leash and harness
- [ ] Poop bags
- [ ] Favorite toy and familiar blanket or bed
- [ ] Crate or car seatbelt harness
- [ ] Any medications or calming aids (prescribed by vet)
- [ ] Recent photo of the dog on your phone (in case of separation)
- [ ] New ID tag with your cell number and Oregon address

**TOOLS AND SUPPLIES (M — pack the night before)**

- [ ] Basic toolkit: Phillips and flathead screwdriver, pliers, adjustable wrench, box cutter, tape measure
- [ ] Packing tape and marker (for last-minute sealing and labeling)
- [ ] First-aid kit
- [ ] Flashlight or headlamp
- [ ] Roll of toilet paper
- [ ] Hand soap or sanitizer
- [ ] All-purpose cleaning spray and a few rags (for quick wipe-down at new place)
- [ ] Zip-lock bags (assorted sizes, endlessly useful)

**CAR EMERGENCY KIT (M — confirm it's in the trunk)**

- [ ] Jumper cables or portable jump starter
- [ ] Tire pressure gauge and portable air inflator
- [ ] Spare tire (confirmed present and inflated)
- [ ] Roadside emergency triangles or flares
- [ ] Rain jacket
- [ ] Blanket
- [ ] Phone mount for navigation

**BEFORE YOU LEAVE THE OLD PLACE (J — do this together)**

- [ ] Walk through every room, open every closet and cabinet
- [ ] Photograph each room, the exterior, and all meter readings
- [ ] Return keys, garage remotes, mailbox keys to landlord (get a receipt or confirmation text)
- [ ] Confirm Ohio utilities are set to shut off tomorrow
- [ ] Lock all doors and windows
- [ ] Take a breath — you're on your way

# ICS CALENDAR FILE

Copy everything below into a plain text editor (Notepad on Windows, TextEdit on Mac set to plain text). Save the file as **move-countdown.ics** — make sure the extension is .ics, not .txt. Then open the file or import it into Google Calendar (Settings → Import & Export → Import) or Apple Calendar (File → Import). Every event will appear on your calendar and you can drag them to the correct dates based on your actual move day.

I've set the events to a placeholder start date of **Monday, July 14, 2025** as Day 56 (8 weeks out), with the move day on **Sunday, September 7, 2025**. If your dates are different, do a find-and-replace on the year/month/day values before importing, or just import and drag the events in bulk. Each event title starts with who's responsible.
